prov.heading: ALLOWANCE FOR CREDIT LOSSES
prov.text:
The ACL represents management's best estimate of lifetime credit losses for loans and leases and unfunded commitments. The ACL totaled $480 million as of September 30, 2026, a decrease of $5 million from $485 million as of December 31, 2025. The change in the ACL estimate during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 reflects the combined effect of updated economic assumptions, portfolio activity and credit migration, and changes to the Company's ACL estimation methodology and qualitative adjustments.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text: The Company's effective tax rate for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 was 24.7% and 24.6%, respectively, as compared to 24.4% for the three months ended June 30, 2026 and 24.9% for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The effective tax rates differed from the statutory federal income tax rate primarily due to the impact of state income taxes, non-deductible compensation, non-deductible FDIC assessments, and income from tax-exempt investment securities and loans. The change in the effective tax rate for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to the corresponding period in the prior year, was primarily attributable to the effects of the acquisition of Pacific Premier in the third quarter of 2025.

net.text: The Company reported net income of $220 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $208 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026. The increase was primarily attributable to a $26 million increase in net interest income and a $5 million decrease in non-interest expense, reflecting lower merger and restructuring expense. These favorable impacts were partially offset by an $8 million decrease in non-interest income, a $6 million increase in provision for credit losses, and a $5 million increase in provision for income taxes. The increase in net interest income primarily reflected higher yields on interest-earning assets, including loans and taxable investment securities, partially offset by lower average interest-earning asset balances. Interest expense declined due to lower average balances of interest-bearing deposits and borrowings.

wc.text: Commercial loans are made to commercial customers for use in normal business operations to finance working capital needs, equipment purchases, or other projects. The Bank focuses primarily on borrowers doing business within our geographic markets, with certain specialty lines of business that operate nationally. Commercial loans are generally underwritten individually and secured with the assets of the company and/or the personal guarantee of the business owners. Lease and equipment financing products are designed to address the diverse financing needs of small to large companies, primarily for the acquisition of equipment. As of September 30, 2026, commercial loans held in our loan portfolio were $12.8 billion, an increase of $815 million, or 9% on an annualized basis, compared to December 31, 2025, driven primarily by relationship-based loan originations.
